name: The Content Engine: 12 Prompts for Solo Founders
tagline: Turn a single core insight into seven days of high-converting social and newsletter content.
metaDescription: Transform one raw product insight into a full week of engaging posts. 12 plug-and-play AI prompts designed specifically for time-strapped solo founders.
description:
Built specifically for bootstrapped and solo founders who cannot afford to spend twenty hours a week writing marketing copy. Most founders struggle with inconsistent publishing not because they lack ideas, but because translating a single product update or customer win into multiple distinct formats is mentally exhausting.

The Content Engine solves distribution fatigue by providing an operational framework for repurposing. Instead of asking AI to create content out of thin air, these 12 prompts deconstruct a single validated insight into distinct strategic angles: tactical teardowns, contrarian opinions, customer proof stories, and high-engagement discussion starters.

Each prompt applies tested copywriting structures, strict constraints against corporate buzzwords, and clear formatting rules. By feeding the system your raw notes once, you generate an entire week's publishing calendar across LinkedIn, X, and your email newsletter in under thirty minutes.
includes: 12 battle-tested prompt templates in Markdown and PDF formats
Plug-and-play input variables with inline founder usage tips
Content distribution schedule matrix for multi-channel planning
Tone-calibration guidelines to eliminate generic AI phrasing
sampleItems: Take this core founder insight: [Insert core idea]. Rewrite it as a contrarian LinkedIn post that challenges a common industry belief. Frame the opening hook around a costly mistake most founders make, followed by three concise bullet points showing an alternative path based on my experience, and finish with an open-ended question to drive comments. Keep sentences under 15 words and maintain a pragmatic tone. Tip: Paste raw, unedited notes into the bracket for the most authentic voice.

Turn this feature or lesson: [Insert update] into a five-part carousel script for visual platforms. Slide 1: High-stakes hook presenting the core problem. Slide 2: Why conventional advice fails. Slide 3: The counterintuitive framework we used to solve it. Slide 4: A concrete real-world example with numbers. Slide 5: One actionable takeaway for the reader today. Tip: Export this text directly into your preferred slide design tool.

items.title: The Contrarian Industry Angle
items.body: Take this core founder insight: [Insert core idea]. Rewrite it as a contrarian LinkedIn post that challenges a common industry belief. Frame the opening hook around a costly mistake most founders make, followed by three concise bullet points showing an alternative path based on my experience, and finish with an open-ended question to drive comments. Keep sentences under 15 words and maintain a pragmatic tone. Tip: Paste raw, unedited notes into the bracket for the most authentic voice.

items.title: The Tactical Step-by-Step Teardown
items.body: Using this workflow: [Insert workflow or technical process], generate an educational post formatted as an actionable tutorial. Structure it with an outcome-driven headline, an immediate one-sentence premise, five numbered sequential steps with zero fluff, and a brief summary of the primary pitfall to avoid. Write for an intermediate practitioner, not a beginner. Tip: Use this to explain how your product actually works under the hood without explicitly pitching it.

items.title: The Vulnerable Failure Retrospective
items.body: Analyze this mistake: [Insert error, bug, or failed launch]. Structure a storytelling post using the 'Challenge-Choice-Consequence' framework. Start with the immediate emotional and operational fallout, describe the exact decision made to address it, and outline the durable policy we adopted as a result. Tone must be humble, objective, and analytical, avoiding humblebrags. Tip: Post this mid-week when social engagement rewards authentic narrative depth over hype.

items.title: The Micro-SaaS Tool Stack Breakdown
items.body: Based on my thesis that [Insert thesis], curate a breakdown of 4 to 5 tools or workflows I use to achieve this outcome. Format each item with: Tool Name, The Exact Job It Performs, and The Time Saved Weekly. Conclude with a one-sentence summary of why simpler stacks beat complex setups. Tip: Tag the tool creators naturally when publishing to increase external reach and partnership opportunities.

items.title: The Customer Transformation Spotlight
items.body: Transform this customer feedback: [Insert raw review or case metric] into a compelling social proof post. Focus 70% of the text on the user's initial roadblock and frustration before discovering the solution, 20% on the structural shift that solved it, and 10% on the final metric achieved. Do not make my product the hero; make the customer the hero. Tip: Anonymize details if client NDAs require it.

items.title: The Viral Short-Form Thread Hook
items.body: Review this core argument: [Insert thesis]. Generate 5 distinct opening hooks for an X thread or short-form post. Variety required: 1 negative hook (what not to do), 1 curiosity gap hook, 1 numerical data-led hook, 1 personal confession hook, and 1 high-stakes prediction hook. Keep each hook under 220 characters. Tip: Pick the hook that creates the strongest emotional reaction for your Monday morning post.

items.title: The Weekly Deep-Dive Essay
items.body: Expand this brief concept: [Insert topic] into an 800-word newsletter issue for technical founders. Include: an engaging opening anecdote, a deep analytical dive into why the problem persists, two visual framework ideas described in text, and an implementation checklist. Adopt a calm, authoritative editorial tone reminiscent of senior industry analysts. Tip: Use this prompt to build your long-term newsletter archive before breaking it into social snippets.

items.title: The Community Debate Igniter
items.body: Take this common dilemma: [Insert technical or business trade-off, e.g., speed vs. technical debt]. Frame a short post presenting two valid, competing schools of thought without taking an absolute side. Ask the audience to defend their preference in the replies based on their current business stage. Tip: Respond to every comment within the first two hours to maximize platform algorithmic distribution.

items.title: The Multi-Slide Visual Carousel
items.body: Turn this feature or lesson: [Insert update] into a five-part carousel script for visual platforms. Slide 1: High-stakes hook presenting the core problem. Slide 2: Why conventional advice fails. Slide 3: The counterintuitive framework we used to solve it. Slide 4: A concrete real-world example with numbers. Slide 5: One actionable takeaway for the reader today. Tip: Export this text directly into your preferred slide design tool.

items.title: The Zero-BS Soft Pitch Bridge
items.body: Connect this educational topic: [Insert topic] to my product offering: [Insert product utility]. Write a high-value educational post that solves 80% of the problem manually, then introduce my product naturally as the tool that automates the remaining 20%. Avoid aggressive sales copy; focus entirely on efficiency gains. Tip: Use this prompt on Fridays when buyers are reflecting on administrative tasks they want to eliminate.

items.title: The First-Principles Mindset Shift
items.body: Examine this routine operational habit: [Insert standard industry practice]. Deconstruct it from first principles to explain why it exists, why modern context makes it obsolete, and how forward-thinking solo operators should rethink it today. Use logical deduction and eliminate jargon. Tip: Great for positioning yourself as a category thought leader rather than merely a software vendor.

items.title: The Open-Metrics Performance Audit
items.body: Take these internal operational stats: [Insert conversion rate, churn metric, or revenue figure]. Draft a transparent 'Building in Public' post explaining the context behind the numbers. Detail one variable that worked unexpectedly well and one variable that lagged expectations. Conclude with the specific operational experiment scheduled for next week. Tip: Extreme candor in public metrics builds deep buyer trust for indie software.
